title: A Narrative Review of Fetal Tumors- I: Diagnosis and Management of Head, Neck, Orbital and Oral Tumors
content: Fetal tumors (benign and malignant) are uncommon, diverse and vary in presentation, time of diagnosis and outcome. Tumors of the head, neck, mouth and eyes are some of the more common and include teratomas, craniopharyngiomas, lipomas, retinoblastomas and tumors of the choroid plexus. Some of these tumors are difficult to diagnose prenatally and indeed are only diagnosed after delivery although they appear first in-utero. With advances in imaging, identifying these tumors prenatally is improving. Because these tumors are uncommon, it would not be unusual for clinicians not to have come across some of them. In this review we present some of the more common fetal tumors including their ultrasound features (with clues on how to make a diagnosis), associated genetic or structural abnormalities, how to monitor and manage affected fetuses, prognosis and recurrence risk which should inform counselling of parents. For most of these tumors, consideration must be given to accurately defining the extent of the lesions with MRI to allow for planned treatment which is commonly in the form of surgical excision. A number of these tumors will require combination therapy of surgical excision and chemotherapy or radiotherapy. The prognosis for most of them is good depending largely in most cases on the involvement of adjacent structures and the effect of the tumors on adjacent structures.
